title: Drastic Automatic Token-Saving Infrastructure
description: Implement 7 automatic token-saving measures targeting the biggest context waste in PRISM sessions. Current infrastructure (945 LOC across 9 hooks) is advisory-only — warns but doesn't truncate. This milestone adds active compression, caching, and output rewriting to achieve 40-70% session token reduction. All hooks must coexist with existing 52+ user hooks and 42+ project hooks. Latency budget: <500ms per hook.

existing_hooks: bash-intercept.sh (234 LOC) — caches build/test/tsc/git, blocks redundant runs
posttooluse-compressor.mjs (87 LOC) — warns on large outputs, no truncation
read-optimizer.mjs (112 LOC) — warns on large files, suggests offset/limit
search-optimizer.mjs (182 LOC) — injects digest paths before Glob/Grep
pretooluse-token-saver.sh (66 LOC) — warns on broad Glob/large Read
read-tracker.mjs (17 LOC) — tracks files read (PostToolUse, no blocking)
cache-writer.mjs (161 LOC) — writes cache entries after successful commands
loop-detector.mjs (47 LOC) — warns on 3+ identical consecutive tool calls
hook_infrastructure: hook-cache.mjs — shared cache utilities (cachePath, readLines, writeLines, appendUniqueLine)
external_tools: RTK (Rust Token Killer) — https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk — CLI proxy, 60-90% Bash output compression
RTK init creates PreToolUse hook + RTK.md instruction file
Windows pre-built binary available from GitHub releases
reference: Claude Code hook API: PreToolUse can return {continue:true}, {decision:'block',reason:''}, {additionalContext:''} — CANNOT modify tool inputs
PostToolUse hooks: can add additionalContext only — CANNOT modify tool output already in context
bash-intercept.sh pattern: block original (exit 2), run compressed version, return via stderr — effectively rewrites commands

forge_triple.protective_hook: token-budget-enforcer.mjs — blocks tool calls when estimated session token usage exceeds threshold, forces /compact
forge_triple.mcp_action: prism_telemetry → getTokenSavingsReport — returns per-hook savings stats from session cache
forge_triple.skill: /token-ledger enhancement — show per-hook savings breakdown, RTK gain integration

units.title: RTK Installation + Integration Verification
units.description: Download RTK Windows binary from GitHub releases. Place in system PATH. Run `rtk init -g` to create the PreToolUse hook. Verify RTK hook coexists with existing PRISM hooks in settings.json — RTK's hook must not conflict with bash-intercept.sh. Test with: `git status`, `git log`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm list`. Compare output size before/after. Verify RTK gain command shows stats. If RTK conflicts with bash-intercept.sh (both try to intercept same commands), configure RTK to handle output compression while bash-intercept.sh handles caching/blocking.

units.title: Bash Output Truncation — tsc Error Deduplication
units.description: Extend bash-intercept.sh (or create new tsc-error-dedup.mjs PostToolUse hook) to deduplicate TypeScript compiler errors. When `npx tsc --noEmit` fails with N errors, many are the same type repeated across files. The hook should: (1) Parse tsc output to extract unique error codes + messages, (2) Group by error code (TS2304, TS2345, etc.), (3) Return summary: 'N unique errors across M files. Top errors: TS2304 (Cannot find name X) — 47 files, TS2345 (Argument type mismatch) — 23 files. Fix TS2304 first — likely a missing import.' This is a PostToolUse hook on Bash that fires when the command contains 'tsc' and the output exceeds 2000 chars. It can't modify the output already in context, but the additionalContext guidance prevents Claude from reading all 200 errors and instead focuses on root causes.
acceptance_criteria: PostToolUse hook fires on tsc commands with large output
Correctly parses tsc error output format (file:line:col - errorTS#### - message)
Groups errors by error code with file count
Identifies root cause errors (missing imports, type mismatches)
additionalContext message under 500 chars with actionable guidance
Does not fire on successful tsc (0 errors)
Hook completes in <200ms
Works on Windows (\r\n line endings)

units.title: Bash Output Truncation — git/npm/vitest Rewriting
units.description: Extend bash-intercept.sh to rewrite verbose commands BEFORE execution using the block-and-replace pattern (exit 2 with stderr output). New rewrite rules: (1) `git diff` without --stat → block, run `git diff --stat` instead, return via stderr with note 'Use git diff -- <file> for full diff of specific file'. (2) `git log` without --oneline → block, run `git log --oneline -15`, return via stderr. (3) `npm install` / `npm ci` → allow but pipe through `tail -3` to only show final summary. (4) `vitest run` without specific file → wrap to capture output, emit only summary line ('Tests: X passed, Y failed, Z total'). Preserve the existing cache-based blocking (don't re-run if cached). These rewrites layer ON TOP of caching — if cache is fresh, serve cache; if stale, run compressed version.
acceptance_criteria: git diff without flags returns --stat summary + guidance
git log without --oneline returns compact format
npm install returns only final 3 lines
vitest run returns pass/fail summary only
Cache-based blocking still takes priority over rewriting
Specific variants preserved: git diff --cached, git diff <file>, vitest run <specific-file>
No regression in existing bash-intercept.sh functionality
All rewrites complete in <500ms overhead

units.title: Read-Once Session Cache
units.description: Extend read-tracker.mjs from a passive PostToolUse tracker to an active PreToolUse blocker. Current state: read-tracker.mjs appends file paths to .claude/cache/files-read (PostToolUse). New behavior: Add a PreToolUse hook on Read that checks .claude/cache/files-read. If the file was already read this session AND the file hasn't been modified since (compare mtime vs cached read-time), block the re-read with: 'FILE ALREADY READ: You read <path> earlier this session. It has not changed. Use your existing knowledge of this file.' Exceptions that should NOT be blocked: (1) File was modified since last read (check mtime), (2) Read has offset/limit params (targeted re-read of specific section), (3) File is in an exemption list (HANDOFF.md, CURRENT_POSITION.md, settings.json — files that change during session). Store read timestamps, not just paths, to support mtime comparison.
acceptance_criteria: PreToolUse Read hook checks files-read cache with timestamps
Re-read of unchanged file blocked with descriptive message
Modified files allowed through (mtime comparison)
Offset/limit reads always allowed (targeted reads)
Exemption list for session-volatile files (HANDOFF.md, settings.json, CURRENT_POSITION.md, MEMORY.md)
Cache entries include read timestamp for mtime comparison
PostToolUse tracker updated to store {path, timestamp, mtime} instead of just path
Hook completes in <100ms (stat call only, no file read)

units.title: Subagent + MCP Output Compression Guidance
units.description: Add two PostToolUse hooks: (1) Agent tool hook: When an Agent result exceeds 3000 chars, inject additionalContext: 'AGENT RESULT COMPRESSION: This subagent returned N chars. Extract only the specific answer/finding you need. Do not echo the full result — summarize in 1-3 sentences.' This prevents the common pattern where Claude receives a 5000-char agent research result and then restates it verbatim. (2) MCP tool hook for prism_* tools: When any mcp__prism* tool returns >2000 chars, inject: 'MCP RESULT: Large response. Extract only the result values you need. Ignore metadata, timestamps, and debug fields.' Wire both as PostToolUse hooks with appropriate matchers.
acceptance_criteria: PostToolUse hook on Agent tool fires when result >3000 chars
PostToolUse hook on mcp__prism* tools fires when result >2000 chars
Both inject concise additionalContext (<200 chars)
Neither fires on small results (avoids noise)
Correct matchers in settings.json (^Agent$ and ^mcp__prism)
Hooks coexist with existing PostToolUse chains
Each hook completes in <50ms (just length check)

units.title: Context-Size Auto-Compact Trigger
units.description: Enhance enforce-auto-compact.py to trigger based on estimated context byte size, not just edit count. Current behavior: triggers at 20/40/55 edit thresholds. New behavior: Track cumulative tool output bytes this session (sum of all Bash output, Read output, Agent results). When estimated context exceeds 60% of window (~600K chars for 1M context), inject urgent compact warning. When it exceeds 75%, BLOCK further tool calls with: 'CONTEXT CRITICAL: Estimated N chars in context (75% of window). Run /compact immediately to avoid context overflow and information loss.' Implementation: PostToolUse hook that accumulates byte counts in .claude/cache/context-bytes. Reset on SessionStart. The byte tracking is approximate (can't know exact context size) but provides early warning before the system auto-compresses and loses critical facts.
acceptance_criteria: PostToolUse hook tracks cumulative output bytes per session
Byte counter stored in .claude/cache/context-bytes
Warning injected at 60% threshold (~600K chars)
Blocking injected at 75% threshold (~750K chars)
Counter resets on SessionStart
Counter excludes small results (<100 chars) to avoid noise
Counter includes all tool types (Bash, Read, Agent, MCP, Glob, Grep)
Latency <50ms (single file read + write)

units.title: Validation Sweep + Token Savings Measurement
units.description: Create a validation script (token-savings-report.mjs) that measures actual token savings from all TOKEN-OPT hooks. The script should: (1) Read RTK gain stats if RTK installed, (2) Count bash-intercept.sh cache hits from session (read .claude/cache/ entries), (3) Count read-once blocks from files-read cache, (4) Count loop-detector warnings, (5) Count context-bytes current level, (6) Generate a summary report. Wire this into the existing /token-ledger skill. Also run a manual validation: start a fresh session, perform typical PRISM work (read files, run tsc, run tests, search codebase), and measure context usage with and without TOKEN-OPT hooks active. Document results in a findings file.

Report includes: RTK savings, cache hits, re-read blocks, loop warnings, context pressure
Report generates in <1 second
/token-ledger skill enhanced to call this report

Results documented with actual character/token counts
